items.title: How high has Connor McDavid climbed in the all-time player rankings?
items.summary: Even without a Stanley Cup, is he making a run at top-10 status? Top-five? Let’s debate it.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Nov 14, 2026; Toronto, Ontario, CAN; Edmonton Oilers forward Connor McDavid (97) warms up before playing the Toronto Maple Leafs at Scotiabank Arena. Mandatory Credit: Dan Hamilton-Imagn Images Connor McDavid continues to lap his competition as a scorer in his era. He’ll likely join Wayne Gretzky by season’s end as the only players to win the Art Ross Trophy seven or more times, and McDavid will soon become the third-fastest player to record 1,300 points. McDavid is only 29. Health permitting, he has many more great seasons left in him. He’ll probably become the sport’s second 2,000-point scorer. But let’s take stock of where he sits on the all-time player ladder so far. Roundtable: If Connor McDavid retired today, where would you rank him on the all-time player list? MATT LARKIN: I think he’s all the way up to No. 5 for me , behind Gretzky, Bobby Orr, Mario Lemieux and Sidney Crosby, as they mirrored many of McDavid’s stupendous individual accolades while also bringing home multiple championships. Stanley Cups aren’t everything, and McDavid is probably the greatest pure talent the sport has ever seen, which is why I’m willing to slot him above Mr. Hockey Gordie Howe, goal-scoring G.O.A.T Alex Ovechkin, Norris Trophy machine Nicklas Lidstrom and unsolvable goaltender Dominik Hasek. But if McDavid wants to make a run at Mount Rushmore, he needs that one missing trophy. PAUL PIDUTTI: I absolutely love this type of debate. It was one of the reasons I created my PPS system: to rank players across eras. Entering 2026-27, McDavid was the No. 7 forward in PPS after only 11 seasons. For me, he’s played at a level topped only by Gretzky, Orr, and Lemieux in terms of unparalleled dominance. But at 29 years old, it’s still a masterpiece in progress

items.summary: Ostlund has five goals and 10 assists for 15 points in 25 games with the Sabres this season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Noah Ostlund could be out for the foreseeable future. Buffalo Sabres head coach Lindy Ruff told reporters after Friday night’s 6-3 loss to the Pittsburgh Penguins that the center has been placed on injured reserve and will miss “at least a month.” Ostlund wasn’t in the lineup as the 22-year-old suffered a lower-body injury from blocking a shot in Buffalo’s 5-1 win over the New York Rangers last Wednesday. In 25 games this season, he has five goals and 10 assists for 15 points. The Sabres are now 11-11-4 with 26 points , sixth in the Atlantic Division and five points back of a Wildcard spot in the Eastern Conference. The team will travel out west for a four-game road trip which kicks off Tuesday against the Edmonton Oilers . Since joining the league in 2024-25, the native of Stockholm, Sweden has 16 goals and 26 assists for 42 points in 93 appearances. He also has a goal and an assist in three Stanley Cup Playoff games. Ostlund was taken by the Sabres with the No. 16 overall pick in the 2022 NHL Entry Draft. In parts of three AHL seasons with the Rochester Americans, he had 22 goals and 25 assists for 47 points in 54 games. He’s also scored a goal and two assists for three points in 11 Calder Cup Playoff games. In parts of three seasons with Djurgardens Jr. in Sweden’s junior league, Ostlund scored 16 goals and added 41 assists for 57 points in 42 games. Before making the jump to North America, he spent one full season in Sweden’s top domestic league, where he scored 12 goals and recorded 11 assists for 23 points in 38 games with Vaxjo HC.

The Edmonton Oilers were gifted eight power plays and lost 4-2 to Seattle, a team that had won just one other time in Rogers Place since coming into the league in 2021 (now 9-2). The Kraken were resilient, hanging around before scoring three third-period goals. But when you’re the Oilers, you feel like the game should have been out of reach by then. Hockey’s best power play over the past half a decade simply didn’t produce. items.title: Suter followed father, uncle's path on way to U.S. Hall of Fame
items.summary: The 2026 U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame induction is Nov. 30. This year's class includes Amanda Kessel, Phil Kessel, T.J. Oshie, Ryan Suter and Stan Wong. Here, NHL.com senior writer Dan Rosen profiles Suter.
items.body: Dedication, grit hallmarks of defenseman's 20-season NHL career The 2026 U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame induction is Nov. 30. This year's class includes Amanda Kessel, Phil Kessel , T.J. Oshie , Ryan Suter and Stan Wong. Here, NHL.com senior writer Dan Rosen profiles Suter. Ryan Suter 's reaction to getting into the U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame is on brand for the former NHL defenseman. Gracious but humble. Never selfish, thinking only about the people that matter most to him and how they feel, how they would react. "People ask me and I'm just like, 'You know, it's cool, but it's more about my family,'" Suter said. "I wish my dad was here because that would be pretty cool for him. My Uncle Gary, my grandparents -- for me, yeah, it's cool, don't get me wrong, it's pretty awesome, but it's more about them." Suter will be inducted at a ceremony at the Grand Hyatt in Washington on Nov. 30. Joining him in the Class of 2026 are fellow Wisconsin natives Phil and Amanda Kessel, former Team USA teammate TJ Oshie, and Stan Wong, a longtime athletic trainer for USA Hockey. Bob Suter, Ryan's father, was inducted in 2003 as a member of 1980 USA "Miracle on Ice" team. Gary Suter, Bob's brother, was inducted in 2011, nine years after ending an NHL playing career that featured 1,145 games as a defenseman with the Calgary Flames, Chicago Blackhawks and San Jose Sharks.​ Ryan said his dad and uncle had the greatest impact on him as a hockey player and he credits them, and his upbringing, for carving out an NHL career that spanned 20 seasons, 696 points (107 goals, 589 assists) in 1,526 games with the Nashville Predators, Minnesota Wild, Dallas Stars and St. Louis Blues. items.title: Oilers drop fifth straight as Kraken rally with three third-period goals
items.body: EDMONTON — Kaapo Kakko scored two third-period goals two minutes apart as the Seattle Kraken rallied to beat the Edmonton Oilers 4-2 on Friday. Jordan Eberle and Vince Dunn also scored and Matty Beniers had a pair of assists for the Kraken (12-10-1), who have won two of their last three and snapped an eight-game road losing skid against the Oilers. Philipp Grubauer made 16 stops before suffering an upper-body injury and being replaced by Joey Daccord, who made nine saves. Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl replied for the skidding Oilers (17-7-4), who lost their fifth in a row. Edmonton went 1-for-8 on the power play. Kraken: Eberle scored his franchise-best 22nd career game-opening goal with Seattle to leave him just one point shy of 800 career NHL points. He became the fifth skater taken in the 2008 NHL draft to reach the milestone. Oilers: McDavid extended his season-opening home point streak to 14 games and became the sixth player in NHL history to reach 60 points in 28 games or fewer — the first since Mario Lemieux did so in 1995-96 in 21 contests. The other ones to hit 60 this early were Wayne Gretzky, Bernie Nicholls, Mike Bossy and Phil Esposito. Edmonton looked to have gone up 3-1 with 23 seconds left in the second period as McDavid blasted the puck into the net on an odd-man rush. However, Draisaitl was given a penalty for interference on the play, a blown call as the replay revealed that Brandon Montour had tripped over his own discarded stick. Edmonton is usually full value when facing the Kraken as they came into the contest with a 16-4-0 record against Seattle and had an eight-game home winning streak dating back to Jan. 17, 2023.

items.title: Kraken’s Philipp Grubauer exits game with upper-body injury
items.summary: Grubauer stopped 16 of 18 shots before being replaced by Joey Daccord after 40 minutes.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The Seattle Kraken confirmed Friday that goaltender Philipp Grubauer left their game against the Edmonton Oilers after sustaining an upper-body injury. Grubauer, 35, was replaced by Joey Daccord between the pipes for Seattle after stopping 16 of 18 shots he faced across the first 40 minutes in Edmonton. The Kraken did not specify exactly when or how Grubauer sustained the injury, but Oilers forward Colton Dach received a two-minute minor penalty for goaltender interference after colliding hard with Grubauer late in the first period. Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl both scored on Grubauer in the second period to give the Oilers a 2-1 lead after 40, but the Kraken ultimately rallied to win by a 4-2 final score off a pair of goals by Kaapo Kakko and one more by Vince Dunn in the third period. As Daccord was in net when the Kraken scored the deciding goal, he was awarded the win for his personal stat line. Entering Friday’s action, Grubauer had posted a 6-5-1 record with an .894 save percentage through 14 appearances with the Kraken to begin the 2026-27 regular season. The German goaltender is in the final year of his contract with the Kraken, which carries a $5.9 million cap hit. The Kraken originally signed Grubauer to a six-year contract as an unrestricted free agent ahead of the 2021-22 season, their inaugural year in the NHL. However, apart from his first year with the club, Grubauer has never received the lion’s share of the starts with the Kraken, although he did appear in all 14 games during the team’s lone playoff appearance to date in 2023. items.summary: The Toronto Maple Leafs have signed prospect Alexander Bilecki to an entry-level contract.
items.body: Register Login Maple Leafs Sign Alexander Bilecki By Brian La Rose | at November 27, 2026 8:59 pm The Maple Leafs have put pen to paper on a contract with one of their more promising prospects. Gold Star’s Dan Milstein, the agent for Alexander Bilecki , announced ( Twitter link ) that his client has signed an entry-level deal with Toronto. The team subsequently confirmed the signing. The 18-year-old defenseman was a second-round pick by Toronto in 2025, going 60th overall out of OHL Kitchener. He had a smaller role in his rookie year in 2024-25 but the hope was that he’d shine with a more prominent role in time. The Maple Leafs appear to be correct on that bet. Last season, Bilecki more than doubled his point total from his rookie campaign, collecting 29 points in 66 games. He then added 11 more in 18 playoff contests as the Rangers won the OHL title before adding three assists in four Memorial Cup games, another tournament that they won. This season, Bilecki has found another gear altogether offensively. Through 24 games this season, he’s already up to five goals and 23 points, impressive numbers for anyone but especially a blueliner. With Bilecki remaining on loan to Kitchener, his deal will technically slide for this season and still have three years on it heading into 2027-28. He’ll likely make his professional debut at the AHL level with the Marlies next season.

Philadelphia made headlines for their cryptic scratching of Michkov against the Vancouver Canucks on Friday for a “violation of team rules,” and we now know what that violation was. According to Sportsnet’s Frank Seravalli , Michkov got into another altercation with a teammate earlier this week during the Flyers’ 7-3 loss to the Washington Capitals . items.body: Florida has won six of eight, added Barkov, Marchand to lineup after injuries WASHINGTON -- The Florida Panthers are starting to feel more like their old selves with each game. The return of Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand from lengthy injury layoffs earlier this week helped the Panthers feel whole again in the locker room and on the ice. And comebacks like their 3-2 win against the Washington Capitals at Capital One Arena on Friday can restore some of that swagger they played with during runs to consecutive Stanley Cup championships in 2024 and 2025. "Obviously, the boys know what it means for him to go out there and battle for him, and he's going to do the same," Allen said. items.body: TAMPA, Fla. — Linus Ullmark stopped 18 shots, Michael Amadio had a goal and two assists and Tim Stutzle scored twice as the Ottawa Senators defeated the Tampa Bay Lightning 6-2 on Friday. Amadio made it 3-0 at 6:20 of the second period while Stutzle grabbed a rebound on an odd-man rush to make it 4-0 at 17:37. Zub and Giroux scored 1:38 apart in the third before Guentzel scored twice in a span of 4:45. Meanwhile, Ivan Demidov inches closer to a return as Montreal looks to get its struggling power play back on track and clean up its execution.
items.body: LAS VEGAS— Any hope that Kaiden Guhle would be available to play against the Vegas Golden Knights on Saturday was erased when the Montreal Canadiens announced on Friday that the defenceman was day-to-day with an upper-body injury. Guhle left almost halfway through Wednesday’s 6-0 loss in Colorado, seconds after being hit from behind and knocked into the boards by Avalanche captain Gabriel Landeskog. He did not return. “It’s a tough loss, a tough guy to replace,” said Canadiens captain Nick Suzuki, who knew that the absence of Mike Matheson had already had its impact on the team’s recent skid. The Canadiens have lost three consecutive games in regulation for the first time since last November and the absence of their most used player—Matheson—has been an undeniable factor in that. Now, without both Matheson and Guhle, rookies Adam Engstrom and David Reinbacher will get more runway while Arber Xhekaj and Alex Carrier will need to be relied on almost as much as Lane Hutson and Noah Dobson typically are. items.body: NEWARK, N.J. — Connor Brown scored the go-ahead goal off a scramble in front with 3:58 remaining to lead the New Jersey Devils to a come-from-behind 5-3 win over the Calgary Flames on Friday. After Brown’s eighth goal, New Jersey had to kill off a penalty to Jonas Siegenthaler with 2:22 to play to preserve the win. The Devils, who are 11-3 at home, had their NHL-leading 10th comeback victory. Luke Hughes scored twice, including an empty-netter with 11 seconds left, and Jack Hughes had a goal and three assists for a four-point game for the seventh time in his career for the Devils. Timo Meier also scored and Jake Allen stopped 26 shots. Matt Coronado, Zach Whitehead and Joel Hanley had goals for the Flames. Devin Cooley had 29 saves. Jack Hughes tied it at 3 as he was falling down near the crease at 12:25 of the third period on assists from Dougie Hamilton and Arseny Gritsyuk. The Flames erased a 2-1 deficit in the second period with goals from Coronato and Whitecloud to grab a 3-2 lead. New Jersey scored twice within 12 seconds at the start of the second period to go ahead 2-1. Luke Hughes scored his eighth goal of the season from Jack Hughes and Hamilton 56 seconds into the period, then Meier had a goal at 1:08. Calgary went up 1-0 on Hanley's second goal of the season in his 12th game. Yegor Sharangovich and Simon Nemec had the assists, with Nemec extending his points streak to a career-high six games. Nemec was traded to the Flames in June. He was drafted by the Devils with the second pick of the 2022 draft and skated in 155 games with New Jersey.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images Tell me if you’ve heard this before. Chris Tanev is injured. During a Friday matinee matchup between the Toronto Maple Leafs and Boston Bruins , Maple Leafs defenseman Chris Tanev suffered a lower-body injury that forced him to leave the game early. Early in the second period, Tanev went back behind his net to retrieve the puck. After delivering a breakout pass, he took a hit from Bruins forward Marc Kastelic. The check didn’t seem all that ferocious, but Kastelic caught Tanev in a soft spot down low, leaving Tanev in distress. Play came to a halt as Tanev needed assistance coming off the ice. He went down to the Leafs’ dressing room and didn’t return to the game. He logged just 7:53 of ice time across 11 shifts. The 36-year-old has seemingly been on the injured list as much as he has actually dressed for the Maple Leafs during his tenure with the Original Six franchise. He already missed nine games due to an upper-body injury back in October, which came after playing just 11 games for the entirety of the 2025-26 campaign. The injury comes just a few days after the Toronto native potted his first goal of the season, scoring in a 4-2 win over the New York Islanders on Tuesday night. Tanev has just two points in 16 appearances this season, registering a plus/minus of -3 while averaging a little over 18 minutes of ice time per game. Tanev has never competed in every regular-season game in his NHL career. In 894 appearances, he has scored 37 goals and 212 points, with another 16 points in 73 Stanley Cup Playoff appearances. items.title: Frost sign Maddy Christian, Clara Yuhn to contracts
items.summary: Christian, who signed a two-year contract, was taken by Minnesota in the third round of the 2026 PWHL Draft.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: PWHL A couple of youngsters have inked their first pro contracts. The 22-year-old was part of a solid draft class for the Frost, as she was taken in the third round, 33rd overall, of the 2026 PWHL Draft. She enters the pro ranks after an exceptional collegiate career at Penn State University. On a Nittany Lions team that also featured big names like Tessa Janecke and Katie DeSa, Christian rounded out her tenure with the program with back-to-back 30-point campaigns. After scoring a career-best 21 goals as a junior, the Elk River, Minn. native set career highs in assists (16) and points (35) last season, helping Penn State reach the NCAA Women’s Frozen Four for the first time in program history. Christian was part of four conference championship teams at Penn State, having been named to Atlantic Hockey America’s Second All-Star Team twice. In 152 games, she posted 46 goals and 38 assists for 84 points. Yuhn earned a one-year contract after she was invited to the Frost’s training camp. She recently finished up a respectable four years at Boston University. While she posted a career-high 22 points as a sophomore, the Grosse Pointe, Mich. native’s most memorable season came in her junior year in 2024-25, where she notched a career-best 11 goals, as the Terriers went on to win the Hockey East championship, earning a spot in the NCAA Tournament for the first time in a decade. items.title: Bruins’ David Pastrnak leaves game against Leafs with lower-body injury
items.summary: Pastrnak appeared to have tweaked something when taking strides during Friday afternoon’s game.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images Not the best news for fans in Beantown. During the first period of a matinee matchup between the Boston Bruins and Toronto Maple Leafs , Bruins forward David Pastrnak appeared to have tweaked something while he was simply skating out of the zone. After a face-off win for Boston, Pastrnak took hard strides as the team tried to break the puck out. However, the Czech sniper looked to be in discomfort when he crossed the blue line, and immediately veered to the Bruins’ bench. Pastrnak slammed his stick as he exited the playing surface before limping down the tunnel toward the team’s dressing room. The Bruins later announced that Pastrnak is “unlikely” to return to Friday’s contest. He logged just 5:50 of ice time across six shifts, putting one shot on goal and blocking another. The average NHL goalie has never been taller.

items.body: Statistical edge due in part to better adjustment against east-west offensive tactics Goalies hit an average of 6-foot-3 for the first time in League history in 2024-25, and after the average dipped by one-tenth of an inch in 2025-26, are right back up to those lofty heights so far this season. That’s an increase of 1.3 inches from 15 years ago, which probably isn’t a shock given the NHL push toward larger goalies who, in theory, take up more of the net. So, what has that rise meant for smaller goalies during the same period? Perhaps surprisingly, the number of goalies playing regularly at 6-foot-1 or shorter has remained somewhat steady during the same 15-year period. Already this season, 18 goalies listed at 6-foot-1 or shorter have appeared in at least one game, and 15 are playing a regular role, same as last season and one below the average across the previous four seasons. That list includes rookies Jacob Fowler of the Montreal Canadiens (6-1), Dylan Garand of the New York Rangers (6-1) and Devon Levi of the Edmonton Oilers (6-0). “Honestly, it's less of a conversation now than it used to be,” said Levi, adding size is not something he discusses with good friends and offseason training partners Garand and Jet Greaves of the Columbus Blue Jackets, a fellow 6-foot goalie. “The game has changed a lot in the past, I don't know, 10 years, and it continues to change, and there's so much more than just being big.” The gap between the number of games played by goalies 6-foot-1 or shorter and goalies 6-foot-5 or taller has shrunk significantly the past 15 years, from 856 games in 2011-12 to an average of 152.2 during the past five seasons, and smaller goalies had only played seven more games this season. items.title: Flyers' Michkov Being Held Out Vs. Canucks Due To 'Internal Team Matter'
items.summary: The 21-year-old will be scratched after reportedly violating team rules.
items.body: David Kirouac-Imagn Images Eric Cruikshank Partner Nov 27, 2026 7:05 PM Published Nov 27, 2026 7:05 PM The 21-year-old will be scratched after reportedly violating team rules. The Philadelphia Flyers' turbulent season just took another dark turn. The Flyers announced on Friday that Matvei Michkov will not be playing against the Vancouver Canucks due to an "internal team matter." Notably, this statement was made by Dan Hilferty, Flyers Governor and CEO of Comcast Spectacor, not GM Daniel Briere or president Keith Jones. This announcement came after Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman initially reported that Michkov had "violated team rules." Michkov's name has been circulating in the rumor mill after ESPN's Kevin Weekes reported on Nov. 10 that the 21-year-old would "likely want a new start elsewhere." Weekes added that he is a prime candidate moving forward. GM Daniel Briere has since come out and refuted any reports surrounding the possibility of Michkov being traded. Speaking with Sportsnet's Frank Seravalli earlier this month, Briere said he did not not receive a request for a trade from Michkov's agent, and that the organization was surprised by Weekes' reporting. Michkov is in the final year of his entry-level contract and is set to become a restricted free agent at the conclusion of the 2026-27 season. The Russian winger leads the Flyers with 11 goals and 20 points in 27 games. Michkov was selected seventh overall by the Flyers in 2023 and has posted 134 points in 188 career games. After starting out the season with seven straight losses and a combined 5-10-5 record through their opening 20 games, the Flyers have since gone 5-2-1 and are five points behind the New York Islanders for the third spot in the Metropolitan Division.

items.title: Sabres’ Zach Benson, Noah Ostlund out against Penguins with injuries
items.summary: Ostlund blocked a shot against the New York Rangers on Wednesday night, while Benson is dealing with an upper-body injury.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Timothy T. Ludwig-Imagn Images A couple of key players on the Buffalo Sabres roster won’t be available on Black Friday. When speaking to the media after morning skate, Sabres head coach Lindy Ruff revealed that forwards Zach Benson and Noah Ostlund won’t be in the lineup, as the team plays host to the lowly Pittsburgh Penguins on Friday night. Benson skated by himself on Friday morning, with Ruff noting that the gritty youngster is dealing with an upper-body injury. Ostlund apparently was hurt when he blocked a shot in the Sabres’ 5-1 win over the New York Rangers on Wednesday night. Ruff didn’t have a timeline for either player. He noted that Ostlund is continuing to be tested by team personnel, as Buffalo is waiting to see if they have to make any decision on calling anyone up from its American Hockey League affiliate, the Rochester Americans. It will lead to some notable shifting in Buffalo’s lineup. Forward Justin Danforth is expected to return to the lineup after missing several games due to a lower-body injury. If the line rushes from morning skate prove anything, it’s that the Sabres are going to use 11 forwards and seven defensemen against the last-place Penguins. Benson has been banged up a little this season, but hasn’t missed a game yet in the 2026-27 campaign. In 25 appearances, the 21-year-old has scored five goals and 18 assists for 23 points, ranking first on the team in helpers, third in points and tied for third in goals. Ostlund has also dressed for every game. He is tied with Benson with five goals thus far, registering 10 assists and 15 points. The Sabres (11-10-4) entered Friday’s action sixth in the Atlantic Division, five points back of the last Wild Card spot in the Eastern Conference.

items.title: Defensive Woes Holding Flyers Back From Salvaging Season
items.summary: The Philadelphia Flyers have had a bounce-back stretch of hockey after a terrible start to the season. However, the team's defensive structure is holding them back.
items.body: David Kirouac-Imagn Images Adam Proteau Partner Nov 27, 2026 6:32 PM Published Nov 27, 2026 6:32 PM The Philadelphia Flyers have had a bounce-back stretch of hockey after a terrible start to the season. However, the team's defensive structure is holding them back. Despite a horrendous start to the season, the Philadelphia Flyers are slowly scratching and clawing their way to back relevancy in the Metropolitan Division. Since they stumbled out to a 5-10-5 record through their opening 20 games, the Flyers have gone 5-2-1, a mark that includes victories over the Ottawa Senators , Buffalo Sabres and Montreal Canadiens . Philadelphia also has benefitted from playing in a weaker division, where elsewhere, their poor start probably would've stamped their fate. If there's one thing that’s hurting Philly more than anything, it's their defense. In their past six games, the Flyers have been outscored 26-23, highlighted by a 7-3 defeat at the hands of the Washington Capitals on Wednesday. The Flyers' 4.33 goals-against average (third-highest in the league in this recent stretch) has to be especially frustrating because the offense has finally come around, with their 3.83 goals-for average ranking seventh in the same span. The Flyers have been without a true No. 1 defenseman for eons now. 30-year-old Travis Sanheim has shown flashes of being that player for them, and despite averaging 24:37 of ice time, he doesn't possess the game-breaking skill that the upper echelon of blueliners around the NHL have showcased. It isn't primarily Sanheim's fault that the Flyers' defense is so porous. Look at Philadelphia's entire defense corps, and you'll see an underwhelming, flawed group of D-men. items.title: Ducks place Leo Carlsson on injured reserve
items.summary: Carlsson was injured last week after running into an official during a game against the Mammoth.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Rob Gray-Imagn Images Some roster management for the team in Orange County, as it trudges through the start of the holiday season without one of its star players. According to the NHL Media Site, the Anaheim Ducks have placed forward Leo Carlsson on injured reserve with an upper-body injury. Carlsson has been out of action since last Saturday, when he was hurt during a game against the Utah Mammoth . During that contest, Carlsson was attempting to get the puck into the offensive zone. He was met with a firm check from Mammoth defenseman Mikhail Sergachev, which led to the two colliding with a linesman at the Utah blue line. Carlsson sat on the ice for a few minutes, with his hands to his face, before being helped off the ice by the Ducks’ training staff. Anaheim went on to lose to the Mammoth, 3-2. The young Swede has already missed the past two contests, which saw the Ducks lose to the Seattle Kraken , before hammering the San Jose Sharks 7-0 on Wednesday night. With Carlsson’s placement on IR retroactive to Nov. 21, he will be forced to miss Anaheim’s home-and-home against the rival Los Angeles Kings , but will be eligible to return to the lineup next Tuesday, when the Ducks welcome the Minnesota Wild to town. After signing his massive new deal prior to the start of the 2026-27 season, the 21-year-old has been a key part of Anaheim’s success in the early going. In 24 appearances, Carlsson has scored seven goals and 22 assists for 29 points, sitting fourth on the team in goals and tied for second in points. The Ducks (12-13-1) come into the weekend third in the Pacific Division, 13 points out of first place.

items.body: Two weeks ago, the Federal Aviation Administration in the United States made a sudden decision to ground all planes, interrupting air travel across the country. This had the potential to throw the sports world into chaos too, as teams were making their way to their next locations. In the end, the schedule carried on as normal for the NHL. There were no game postponements and everyone got to where they needed to be. The NFL's games went on as planned too, but there was at least one element affected when officiating assignments had to be overhauled. Four NFL refs had to officiate two games on the same day. Starting with an afternoon Dolphins-Colts game in Indianapolis, the refs then had to drive to Cincinnati to be ready for an 8:20 p.m. ET start time for the Steelers-Bengals game. In the end, the nationwide grounding lasted a little over four hours and the sports world was not affected on a greater scale. But what if it went on longer and had a wider-ranging impact? items.title: Ukraine urges countries to follow Canada’s lead in barring Russian athletes
items.body: Ukraine's sports minister wants other countries to follow Canada's lead in blocking Russian teams from international hockey tournaments. Matviy Bidnyi, in an op-ed published Friday by the Ukrainian news agency RBC-Ukraine, credited diplomatic efforts by Ukrainian government officials for Canada's decision to bar Russian players from next month's world junior hockey championship in Edmonton and Red Deer, Alta. Bidnyi said he is pushing for similar restrictions in other countries to prevent Russia's return to international hockey. Prime Minister Mark Carney said earlier this month that Russian players would not be permitted to compete in Canada as long as Russia's war in Ukraine continues. The International Ice Hockey Federation announced Wednesday it would challenge a Court of Arbitration for Sport ruling ordering the reinstatement of Russian teams to five international championships. Russia and Belarus have been barred from international hockey since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, and several European federations have vowed to boycott games if Russia is allowed to compete.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Brad Penner The New York Islanders announced Friday that forward Kyle Palmieri will be out six-to-eight months with a torn ACL and meniscus in his right knee. He’s also appeared in 68 career Stanley Cup Playoff games, where he’s recorded 18 goals and 14 assists for 32 points. He was part of the Ducks’ and Islanders’ conference final runs in 2015 and 2021, respectively. items.body: Defenseman played 1,048 games, including for Panthers, Wild last season Jeff Petry announced his retirement from the NHL after 16 seasons on Thursday. The 38-year-old defenseman had nine assists in 67 games with the Florida Panthers and Minnesota Wild last season. He did not have a point in three Stanley Cup Playoff games. Petry made the announcement on his wife's podcast "Never Offside with Julie & Cat." Selected by the Edmonton Oilers in the second round (No. 45) of the 2006 NHL Draft, Petry had 394 points (96 goals, 298 assists) in 1,048 regular-season games for the Edmonton Oilers, Montreal Canadiens, Pittsburgh Penguins, Detroit Red Wings, Panthers and Wild. He had 13 points (five goals, eight assists) in 51 playoff games and made the Cup Final with the Canadiens in 2020-21 when they lost to the Tampa Bay Lightning in five games. Petry played in his 1,000th game while with the Panthers last season against the Vancouver Canucks on Nov. 17, 2025. "Playing 1,000 games going into last year, that was a goal of mine and to be able to accomplish that was great," he said. The Ann Arbor native, who got to play for his hometown Red Wings for two seasons from 2023-25, also discussed some of his favorite NHL memories. "My first (NHL) game in Edmonton (Dec. 28, 2010)," Petry said. "That dream finally came true. Scoring my first goal (Jan. 20, 2011). The biggest memory was playing in the finals with Montreal. Obviously not the ending result (we wanted), but to be able to do that was special." Petry also represented the United States at the IIHF World Championships four times (2012-2014, 2024), including winning the bronze medal in 2013. items.summary: The 2026 U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame induction is Nov. 30. This year's class includes Amanda Kessel, Phil Kessel, T.J. Oshie, Ryan Suter and Stan Wong. Here, NHL.com senior draft writer Mike Morreale profiles Phil Kessel.
items.body: 3-time Cup champ holds ironman streak with 1,064 straight regular-season games The 2026 U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame induction is Nov. 30. This year's class includes Amanda Kessel, Phil Kessel , T.J. Oshie , Ryan Suter and Stan Wong. Here, NHL.com senior draft writer Mike Morreale profiles Phil Kessel. Phil Kessel played through the pain, the bumps, the bruises and all those mornings when he arrived at the rink just not feeling right. He’d play 1,064 consecutive regular-season games, in fact, an NHL Ironman record built over nearly 13 years and five teams. He played through injuries others never knew about, the pressure of being a star and three long Stanley Cup Playoffs runs. Kessel never set out to chase the record. In an interview with NHL Network Radio and during his election press conference, he said he simply hated sitting out. "I don't think it was ever a priority," Kessel said. "I just always wanted to play in the games. I love playing the games. I love playing hockey and I never wanted to miss. "As a player and competitor, you never want to sit out. You never want to be in the stands. You never want to be injured. You always want to be out there." That passion, durability and understated competitiveness helped make Kessel one of the most accomplished American players of his generation. Now, the reluctant superstar and three-time Stanley Cup champion is headed to the U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame. Kessel and his sister, Amanda, an Olympic gold medalist and four-time IIHF Women's World Championship gold medalist, headline the Class of 2026 to be inducted at the dinner and ceremony at the Grand Hyatt Washington in Washington, D.C., on Nov. 30. The Madison, Wisconsin, natives will become the second sister-brother combination inducted, joining Cammi Granato and Tony Granato.

In the video accompanying the announcement, it was noted that Dillon was deemed to have elevated “upward and unnecessarily and making Mateychuk’s head the main point of contact on a hit where such head contact was avoidable” . items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images The Montreal Canadiens suffered a 6-0 defeat at the hands of the Colorado Avalanche on Wednesday, but the total loss for Canadiens winger Florian Xhekaj, specifically, is just a bit larger. On Thursday, the NHL Department of Player Safety announced that they have fined Xhekaj $2,426.98, the maximum allowable amount under the collective bargaining agreement (CBA), for his trip of Avalanche forward Fedor Svechkov during Wednesday’s game. There was a total of 57 penalty minutes assessed in the game, with the Xhekaj brothers accounting for 33 of them. This is the 22-year-old Florian Xhejak’s first instance of league-levied discipline. items.body: New Jersey Devils defenceman Brenden Dillon received a four-game suspension on Thursday for an illegal hit to the head of Columbus Blue Jackets defenceman Denton Mateychuk. Dillon was assessed a match penalty for the check during the first period of the Devils' shootout win in Columbus on Wednesday night. Mateychuk left the game after the hit. Dillon forfeits $82,474.24 based on his average annual salary and under the terms of the collective bargaining agreement. The money goes to the Players’ Emergency Assistance Fund. On the play, Mateychuk skated through neutral ice and entered the zone before moving the puck to a teammate. Once the puck was gone, Dillon finished a “high, hard check, elevating upward and unnecessarily and making Mateychuk's head the main point of contact on a hit where such head contact was avoidable,” the NHL's department of player safety said in a video. Blue Jackets coach Rick Bowness said after the game: "I’ve coached Dillon. He’s not a dirty player. He’s a hard player. He caught him in a bad spot, and that’s a bad hit. It is.” Bowness said Wednesday that he spoke with Mateychuk and the defenceman “feels fine.” Bowness added that “protocol will take over and we’ll go from there.”

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Nick Wosika-Imagn Images The Minnesota Wild are in a tough spot. Just under a year after mortgaging a sizeable chunk of their future to land star defenseman Quinn Hughes from the Vancouver Canucks , the Wild seem no closer to signing the 27-year-old to a new contract. If anything, Wild general manager Bill Guerin sounds less and less confident each time he’s asked about the situation. And yet … from a hockey standpoint, the Wild haven’t given Hughes any reason not to sign with them. As of Thursday, they’re tied with the Carolina Hurricanes atop the NHL standings with 41 points. They’ve won 18 of 27 games this season, along with just four regulation losses. Right now, they have to be the odds-on favorites to come out of the Western Conference. Hughes has missed Minnesota’s last three games with an undisclosed injury, but it shouldn’t be long before he returns to the lineup — and when he’s played, the Wild have given him more freedom than ever. The 5’10” righty has already amassed 34 points (eight goals, 26 assists) in 24 games this season, good for second on the Wild in scoring. He’s also averaging a career-high 27:49 of ice time per game. When healthy, Hughes is right there with Cale Makar in the Norris Trophy race every single year, and Hughes will likely continue to be the standard against which all undersized puck-moving defense prospects are measured until the day he retires. He’s as elusive and dangerous as any player in the league. The Wild have a ton of money coming off the books after this season, and you can bet they’d love nothing more than to give most of it to Hughes. Guerin and Wild owner Craig Leipold already made a big statement last year by making Kirill Kaprizov the highest-paid player in the game, at least for a moment.

The disappointing result from last year had a bit to do with injuries but there was also a lack of true top-end talent beyond James Hagens and Cole Hutson. This year's team might face similar struggles, but they do have a bit of a deeper roster, at least up front. items.title: Tanner Jeannot, Tyrel Bauer fight was easily the best of 2026-27
items.summary: The fisticuffs at center ice between Tyrel Bauer and Tanner Jeannot brought back some old-time hockey vibes at TD Garden.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Fighting might not be as popular as it once was in the NHL, but the 2026-27 season has delivered plenty of highlight-reel, viral fisticuffs through the first quarter and beyond, up to U.S. Thanksgiving. On Wednesday night, Winnipeg Jets defenseman Tyrel Bauer and Boston Bruins winger Tanner Jeannot offered one of the season’s best bouts, dropping the gloves for an over-minute fight at center ice at Boston’s TD Garden. The Jets went on to win 4-2, but it wasn’t the result that most will remember from this game. On Thursday’s episode of Daily Faceoff LIVE , co-hosts Tyler Yaremchuk and Carter Hutton dove into the fight that took sports headlines on U.S. Thanksgiving eve. Tyler Yaremchuk: Was this the fight of the year last night? This is some good old-school hockey here. It’s Tyrel Bauer and Tanner Jeannot at center ice at TD Garden; I love the look of this with the big B in the middle. This was just again. This is almost like what you would see every second night when you played in the AHL. Carter Hutton: Yeah, this was it, man. I remember living with Brandon Bollig, who was our fighter with the Rockford IceHogs, and I would complain about my hips being sore from playing too often. Meanwhile, he’s icing his knuckles and fighting every single night. This was a heavyweight bout, man. These guys stood at center ice at TD Garden and absolutely threw. Early in the fight, Bauer gets him and spins him around. For Jeannot to come back with that quick spin and regrip and then throw it at him is world-class, man. This is a great fight. This isn’t for everybody, but it is a way to protect your teammates. This is how you police the game, what happens in the NHL, and why these guys still have jobs, in my opinion. items.title: Checking in on the NHL playoff picture at U.S. Thanksgiving
items.summary: American Thanksgiving has long served as an unofficial measuring stick to gauge teams’ likelihood of making the playoffs. Emily Sadler evaluates the NHL’s post-season picture.
items.body: It’s American Thanksgiving. Do you know where your NHL team is? The U.S. holiday has long served as an unofficial measuring stick to gauge teams’ likelihood of making the playoffs. Put simply, clubs sitting in playoff position at this time of year have a roughly 75 per cent chance of remaining there by season’s end. While far from a perfect rule, it’s generally pretty accurate. Take the past two seasons, for example — of the 16 teams inside the playoff window at Thanksgiving in back-to-back years, 12 ultimately clinched a spot. The rate was higher in 2022-23 and 2023-24, with 13 sitting and staying in a playoff spot. To round out our five-year sample size of recent examples, the 2021-22 campaign also showed a 75 per cent clinch rate of teams in playoff position at the U.S. Thanksgiving mark. When we think about noteworthy exceptions to this benchmark, the 2018-19 St. Louis Blues always jump to mind. By Thanksgiving of that season, the team was sitting last in the Central, lagging seven points behind the Dallas Stars for the second wild card spot, and had just made a coaching change by firing Mike Yeo and promoting Craig Berube in his place. (Of course, what made that squad particularly special was the fact they remained in last place early into the new calendar year, not launching their dramatic and historic comeback until January.) While the Blues are the most extreme case, the past five years show some interesting instances, too — just look at last year’s standings. The 2025-26 Buffalo Sabres brought us the closest thing to those 2018 Blues, sitting last in the Eastern Conference by November’s end, five points outside of the final wild card spot. The 26-year-old found himself in a new jersey just one day before the 2026-27 regular season began after he was dealt by the Columbus Blue Jackets . items.title: Zdeno Chara joins Hockey Hall of Fame selection committee
items.summary: Chara played 24 seasons in the NHL and won the Stanley Cup in 2011, as well as the Norris Trophy in 2009.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images The Hockey Hall of Fame announced Thursday that former NHL defenseman Zdeno Chara has been appointed to its selection committee . Chara, who was inducted into the Hall of Fame in 2025, will replace fellow inductee Igor Larionov. The Hall of Fame selection committee has 18 members and each serves a 15-year term. “It’s a true honor to be asked to serve on the Hockey Hall of Fame Selection Committee,” said Chara. “This game has given me so much throughout my life, and I take seriously the responsibility of helping recognize the individuals who have shaped its history and legacy. I am grateful for this opportunity.” The New York Islanders selected Chara in the third round of the 1996 NHL Draft. Throughout his 24-year NHL career, he skated with the Islanders, Ottawa Senators , Boston Bruins and Washington Capitals . A Slovak native, he recorded 209 goals and 471 assists for 680 points and 2,085 penalty minutes. At 1,680 career regular-season games, he ranks seventh on the NHL’s all-time games played list, and is 36th in points among NHL defenders. He reached the 50-point mark three times in his career and recorded a career-high 19 goals in 2008-09. He also finished with 40 assists and 52 points in 2011-12. He also dressed in 200 playoff games, where he scored 18 goals and added 52 assists for 70 points. He captained the Bruins to a Stanley Cup championship in 2011 and helped them reach the Final in both 2013 and 2019. Chara won the Norris Trophy in 2008-09 and was a five-time finalist in his career. Chara was inducted in 2025 along with Joe Thornton, Duncan Keith, Jennifer Botterill and Brianna Decker. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Longtime NHL defenseman Jeff Petry is hanging up his skates, announcing his retirement from the league at 38 on a recent episode of the “Never Offside” podcast with his wife, Julie and Cat Toffoli, wife of San Jose Sharks forward Tyler Toffoli. Petry had not played at all in 2026-27, last lacing up in 2025-26 when he netted eight assists in 58 games across time with the Florida Panthers and Minnesota Wild . In the three years prior, he also played for the Pittsburgh Penguins and Detroit Red Wings . Yet, he is best known for his time with the Edmonton Oilers and Montreal Canadiens . Selected 45th overall by Edmonton in 2006, he played parts of five seasons in Alberta before the Canadiens acquired him in 2015, where he established himself as a consistent two-way blueline presence. During his time with the Canadiens, he posted four back-to-back seasons with 40 or more points from 2017-18 to 2020-21, with his career high a 13-goal, 33-assist campaign while playing all 82 games in 2018-19. His contributions, largely in front of recently inducted Hockey Hall of Fame netminder Carey Price, helped the Canadiens reach the 2020-21 Stanley Cup Final in the NHL’s second COVID-19-impacted season, where they fell to the Tampa Bay Lightning . The Ann Arbor, Mich., native wraps up his career with 96 goals and 394 points in 1,048 regular-season games, split between the Oilers, Canadiens, Penguins, Red Wings, Panthers and Wild. He also made his presence known internationally, suiting up for the USA four times at the IIHF World Championship, claiming a bronze medal at the 2013 tournament in Sweden and Finland. items.title: Hockey Hall of Fame appoints Zdeno Chara to selection committee
items.body: A recent Hockey Hall of Fame inductee will help decide who joins him. Zdeno Chara has been appointed to the Hockey Hall of Fame's selection committee, they announced on Thursday. Chara, who was added to the hall with the 2025 class in his first year of eligibility, played in the NHL for 24 seasons and became a Stanley Cup champion with the Boston Bruins in 2011. In 2009, he was awarded the James Norris Memorial Trophy for his outstanding year with the Bruins. He was a six-time NHL All-Star and captained the Bruins for 14 seasons. The 49-year-old will take the spot of fellow Hall of Famer Igor Larionov, whose 15-year term serving on the committee has ended. The committee is made up of 18 members who determine who will be added to the hall each November.

items.title: NHL Rumor Roundup: Simon Edvinsson Trade Rumors Heating Up
items.summary: Trade rumors are heating up around Simon Edvinsson as the Dec. 1 deadline for signing the Detroit Red Wings defenseman draws near.
items.body: Brian Bradshaw Sevald-USA TODAY Sports Lyle Richardson Partner Nov 26, 2026 3:40 PM Published Nov 26, 2026 3:40 PM Trade rumors are heating up around Simon Edvinsson as the Dec. 1 deadline for signing the Detroit Red Wings defenseman draws near. Less than a week remains for the Detroit Red Wings to decide the fate of restricted free-agent defenseman Simon Edvinsson. They will either have the 23-year-old under contract by the Dec. 1 deadline for RFA signings, ship him to another team in a sign-and-trade move, or let him play out the season in Sweden and try to sign or trade him next summer. Edvinsson’s future has been an ongoing subject of media speculation . With Dec. 1 fast approaching, the rumors are ramping up. TSN's Darren Dreger reported Tuesday that six or seven teams were said to be in the mix for Edvinsson. He believes they include the San Jose Sharks , Boston Bruins , Toronto Maple Leafs , Utah Mammoth , and the Nashville Predators could be among the suitors along with perhaps the Carolina Hurricanes. items.body: Register Login Have Fights And Scrums After Clean Hits Become An Issue? By Ryan Long | at November 26, 2026 9:39 am A fight between two willing players, or a response to a dirty hit, is part of how hockey polices itself and part of what makes it special. But something has changed in how players react to legal hits. The old approach was to spring into action after an egregious or illegal hit and, after a big clean hit on a teammate, remember the number and settle it later. Now the reflex is to go after the hitter the moment the whistle blows, often halfheartedly, whether the hit was clean or not. So have fights and scrums after clean hits become an issue? The numbers say they have, and the league has had a tool to deal with them for more than three decades. A Pro Hockey Rumors review of NHL play-by-play data from all 399 regular-season games through Nov. 25 found 110 fights. Forty-three of them, or 39.1%, came within 10 seconds of a hit that drew no penalty, with no faceoff in between. In 32 of those 43 fights, one of the combatants was the player who delivered the hit. The instigator penalty was called seven times in those 43 fights. Only eight instigator penalties have been called league-wide this season. In 28 of the 43, the responding team received no penalty beyond the matching fighting majors. The fights are only part of it. Another 60 unpenalized hits this season were followed by roughing calls but no fight. That’s 1.4 of those scrums for every fight after a legal hit, and none of them show up in fight totals. items.title: NHL Coach Hot Seat Index: Who’s on the chopping block?
items.summary: More seasons than not, we see bench bosses fired before Christmas. Who’s in danger?
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources American Thanksgiving represents a fascinating point in the NHL season because the sample sizes are large enough to matter for struggling teams, yet the season is just young enough that it’s still possible to save it in rare cases. The most famous example: the 2018-19 St. Louis Blues, who named Craig Berube interim head coach in November and rose from dead last in the NHL standings as late as Jan. 2 to winning the Stanley Cup. Maybe a case study like that gives teams false hope, maybe not. But we do frequently see firings start to pop up around this time of year in the NHL. In 2023-24, we saw four head coach firings before the league reached its late-December holiday break. The 2024-25 season had four bench bosses axed between Nov. 19 and Dec. 26 alone. The first pink slip of 2025-26 came in mid-January. Recent history thus tells us it’s not too soon to run a temperature check of every seat in the league. Which coaches are in the most trouble right now? These bench bosses are going strong, with no job jeopardy whatsoever based on current results and/or being new hires. Nothing to discuss here.
